- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.15), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% if recent price is rising.  
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 7 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days of decline after peak), reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates in high-sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment > 0.15 over last 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model tends to lag; forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend if sentiment is trending.
